propositions.text: I dismiss this appeal.
propositions.quote: I dismiss this appeal.

propositions.text: The Appellant is a citizen of Nigeria.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX (Appellant) is a citizen of Nigeria.

propositions.text: The Appellant fears risk of torture or death in Nigeria by President Buhari and supporters.
propositions.quote: The Appellant fears that if he returns to Nigeria he is at risk of torture or death at the hands of the President Muhammadu Buhari and his supporters.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant not credible on material aspects of his claim.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) found that the Appellant is not a credible witness with respect to material aspects of his claim.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD breached natural justice and procedural fairness.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the RPD breached natural justice and procedural fairness

propositions.text: The issues are whether the RPD breached natural justice and procedural fairness and erred in credibility finding.
propositions.quote: The determinative issues for the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) are whether the RPD breached the principles of natural justice procedural fairness, and whether the RPD erred in finding that the Appellant is not credible in his claim.

propositions.text: I find no breach of natural justice or procedural fairness by the RPD and no error in credibility finding.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD did not breach natural justice and procedural fairness. I further find that the RPD did not err in finding that the Appellant is not credible in his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal, finds the Appellant fears torture in Nigeria, the RPD found him not credible, and no breach or error occurred.

propositions.text: I dismiss the appeal and find the RPD was correct that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal. The RPD was correct in finding that the Appellant is neither a Convention1 refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal, agreeing with the RPD that the Appellant is not a refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges his father was persecuted in Nigeria in the 1980s for political opinion by Buhari's military regime.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that his father suffered persecution in Nigeria because of his political opinion at the hands of the military regime headed by General Muhammadu Buhari during the 1980s.

propositions.text: The Appellant says his father was imprisoned and tortured for his political beliefs.
propositions.quote: The Appellant says his father was imprisoned because of his political beliefs and tortured while in prison.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges his father was persecuted, imprisoned, and tortured in Nigeria in the 1980s for political opinions.

propositions.text: The Appellant says his father was poisoned by the military regime in 1988 but survived.
propositions.quote: The Appellant says his father was poisoned by the military regime in the XXXX of 1988 but survived.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant says his father was poisoned by the military regime in 1988 but survived.

propositions.text: In 1988, the Appellant fled Nigeria to the US with his father and brothers, traveling on his father's passport as a minor.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 1988, the Appellant fled Nigeria to the United States (US) together with his father and brothers. The Appellant says that he travelled on his father's passport because he was a minor.

propositions.text: The Appellant's father and brothers received refugee protection in the US, but the Appellant did not because he was a minor.
propositions.quote: The Appellant says that his father and brothers received refugee protection in the US, but he did not receive refugee protection because he was a minor.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant fled Nigeria to the US in 1988 with family, traveling on his father's passport as a minor; father and brothers got refugee protection but he did not.

propositions.text: The Appellant lived in the US nearly 30 years, married a US citizen, had three children, and worked as XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: The Appellant lived in the USA for nearly 30 years. He married a US citizen and had three children. For several years the Appellant worked as a XXXX XXXX in the US.

propositions.text: The Appellant says he could not regularize immigration status because his legal entry record was in his father's lost passport.
propositions.quote: The Appellant says that he was unable to regularize his immigration status in the US because the record of his legal entry into the US is recorded in his father's passport which he is unable to locate.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant lived in the US nearly 30 years, married, had children, worked, but could not regularize status due to lost passport record.

propositions.text: The Appellant remained in the US until 2018 when he crossed into Canada and applied for refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The Appellant remained in the US until XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018 when he crossed the border into Canada and applied for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant fears risk of torture or death in Nigeria by President Buhari and supporters if returned.
propositions.quote: The Appellant fears that if he returns to Nigeria, he is at risk of torture or death at the hands of the President Buhari and his supporters.

propositions.text: Buhari returned to power in 2015 as democratically elected president and was re-elected.
propositions.quote: Buhari returned to power in 2015 as the democratically elected president of Nigeria and has subsequently won re-election.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant entered Canada in 2018 seeking refugee protection, fearing torture in Nigeria by Buhari's government, which returned to power in 2015.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD Panel breached natural justice and procedural fairness in the hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the RPD Panel breached natural justice and procedural fairness in the conduct of the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges reasonable apprehension of bias by the RPD Panel.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that: a. There is a reasonable apprehension of bias on the part of the RPD Panel;

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD erred by not adjourning the hearing to allow rest after exclusion consideration.
propositions.quote: b. The RPD erred in not adjourning the hearing after the consideration of exclusion in order to give the Appellant an opportunity to recover and rest.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges the RPD Panel breached natural justice, showed bias, and erred by not adjourning the hearing for rest.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD Member was biased and negative after hearing irrelevant exclusion evidence and exchanges with counsel.
propositions.quote: We respectfully submit that after hearing the irrelevant evidence in the exclusion phase of the hearing, as well as the exchanges with Appellant's Counsel in response to the various objections to the evidence and arguments, the RPD Member entered the inclusion phase with a biased and negative view both of the Claimant and his counsel.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD Member was biased and negative after exclusion phase evidence and counsel exchanges.

propositions.text: The Appellant cites test for bias as whether a reasonable person would conclude bias against him.
propositions.quote: The Appellant cites jurisprudence that the relevant test is whether a reasonable person would conclude that the RPD Panel was biased against the Appellant.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues a reasonable person would find bias against him due to his appearance and speech.
propositions.quote: We submit that a [sic] any reasonable person who would have been confronted to the facts as presented to the RPD member in the exclusion phase and would contemplate the Claimant, a tall, muscular African retired XXXX with a slurred and slow speech, would conclude that it was more likely that the Board Member was biased against him.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues a reasonable person would find the RPD biased against him based on his appearance and speech.

propositions.text: I find no evidence the RPD Panel exhibited bias against the Appellant after reviewing transcript and audio.
propositions.quote: I have examined the transcript and the audio recording of the RPD hearing. I find no evidence that the RPD Panel exhibited bias against the Appellant.

propositions.text: The exchange between RPD Panel and Appellant's Counsel was respectful and appropriate.
propositions.quote: I find that the exchange between the parties was respectful and appropriate.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence of bias by the RPD Panel and that exchanges with counsel were respectful and appropriate.

propositions.text: The RPD Panel explained hearsay evidence is admissible and must be weighed appropriately.
propositions.quote: The RPD Panel explained that hearsay evidence is not inadmissible at the RPD. The RPD Panel further explained that the Minister can present such evidence to the RPD as the Minister considered appropriate, however the RPD Panel was obligated to consider the Minister's evidence and decide what weight, if any, to give the Minister's evidence.

propositions.text: Appellant's Counsel was dissatisfied but the RPD Panel remained respectful and appropriate.
propositions.quote: The audio recording indicates that Appellant's Counsel was dissatisfied with the RPD Panel's position. I find that the RPD Panel was respectful and appropriate throughout the exchange.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD Panel properly explained hearsay rules and remained respectful despite counsel's dissatisfaction.

propositions.text: Minister's Counsel withdrew exclusion application after Appellant's testimony on raised issues.
propositions.quote: Minister's Counsel withdrew the application for exclusion after hearing the Appellant's testimony regarding the issues that the Minister had raised.

paragraphs.summary: Minister's Counsel withdrew exclusion application after Appellant's testimony on relevant issues.

propositions.text: No reasonable person familiar with RPD role and rules would find the Panel biased against the Appellant.
propositions.quote: I find that there is nothing in the record to support a finding that a reasonable person, who was familiar with role of the RPD and the rules that apply to RPD hearings, would conclude that the RPD Panel was biased against the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no reasonable person would conclude the RPD Panel was biased against the Appellant.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by consolidating exclusion and inclusion phases of the hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that: "The Board Member decided to consolidate both the inevitable favorable decision on exclusion with what was then to be a new hearing on inclusion. We submit this was flawed."

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by consolidating exclusion and inclusion hearing phases.

propositions.text: RPD hearings usually consider exclusion and then substance of fear or risk in one proceeding when reasonable.
propositions.quote: RPD hearings are intended to consider the entirety of a claimant's case for refugee protection when it is reasonable to do so. It is usual for the RPD Panel to consider matters such as the possibility of exclusion and then to consider the substance of a claimant's fear of persecution or a risk of section 97 harm.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RPD hearings usually consider exclusion and substantive issues together when reasonable.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD hearing took seven hours.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the RPD hearing took seven hours.

propositions.text: The hearing lasted four hours and 11 minutes, not seven hours, and is not unreasonable in context.
propositions.quote: I have examined the transcript and the audio recording of the RPD hearing. I find that the hearing took a total of four hours and 11 minutes over the course of a full day. The Appellant has not submitted any evidence that such a hearing is unusual in the context of Canadian jurisprudence or that it is unreasonable in the circumstances particular to the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant claims the hearing lasted seven hours; the court finds it lasted four hours and 11 minutes and was reasonable.

propositions.text: The RPD Panel offered breaks and confirmed the Appellant was okay; no refusal of breaks or accommodation requests noted.
propositions.quote: The transcript shows that the RPD Panel offered the Appellant breaks as required and asked the Appellant to confirm that he was okay. The Appellant was represented at the RPD hearing by experienced Counsel. The transcript does not indicate that the RPD Panel refused breaks when requested. Counsel did not advise the RPD Panel that the Appellant required accommodation at the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD Panel offered breaks and no accommodation requests were made or refused.

propositions.text: The RPD Panel did not err in hearing conduct and did not breach procedural fairness or natural justice.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD Panel did not err in the conduct of the RPD hearing. I find that the RPD Panel did not breach procedural fairness and natural justice.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error or breach of procedural fairness or natural justice by the RPD Panel in the hearing conduct.

propositions.text: My role is to assess all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

propositions.text: I have conducted an independent assessment of the evidence and arguments.
propositions.quote: As part of my analysis, I have conducted an independent assessment of the evidence and the arguments.

paragraphs.summary: The court states its role is to independently assess evidence and decide if the RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: Sworn allegations before the IRB are presumed true unless there is reason to doubt their truthfulness.
propositions.quote: When a person swears to the truth of certain allegations before the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB), there is a presumption that those allegations are true unless there is a reason to doubt their truthfulness.

propositions.text: Presumption does not apply to inferences, conclusions, or speculation without evidentiary basis.
propositions.quote: This presumption of truthfulness does not apply to inferences or conclusions a witness may draw from facts, or to speculation for which there is no evidentiary basis.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that sworn allegations before the IRB are presumed true unless doubted, but this presumption excludes inferences or speculation without evidence.

propositions.text: Presumption of truthfulness may be rebutted by contradictions, inconsistencies, omissions, vague testimony, limited knowledge, or reliance on false documents.
propositions.quote: The presumption that a person's sworn testimony is true may be rebutted where problems are identified with the testimony. These problems can include contradictions, inconsistencies, and omissions; incoherent or vague testimony; limited knowledge of key elements of the case; or a reliance on false documents.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains that testimony's presumption of truth can be rebutted by contradictions, omissions, vagueness, limited knowledge, or false documents.

propositions.text: Claimants must provide credible evidence of serious persecution risk on a Convention ground or risk of section 97 harm on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: In order to succeed in a claim for refugee protection, claimants must adduce sufficient credible evidence to establish that they face a serious possibility of persecution on a Convention ground. In the alternative, claimants can succeed by adducing sufficient credible evidence to establish that, on a balance of probabilities, they would be subjected personally to a risk of a section 97 harm.

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimants must show credible evidence of persecution risk or risk of section 97 harm to succeed in refugee claims.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant not credible on material aspects of his refugee claim due to unexplained omissions in his Basis of Claim form.
propositions.quote: The RPD Panel found that the Appellant was not a credible witness with respect to material aspects of his refugee claim. The RPD found that there were important omissions in his Basis of Claim (BOC) form relative to his testimony that were not reasonably explained.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant not credible due to unexplained omissions in his Basis of Claim form.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by making credibility findings on secondary and peripheral issues to the claim.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the RPD Panel erred by making credibility findings on issues that the Appellant argues are secondary and peripheral to the Appellant's claim.

propositions.text: The court disagrees that the RPD erred regarding credibility findings on omissions not explained by the Appellant's profession.
propositions.quote: I do not agree that the RPD Panel erred for the reasons that follow. Omissions from his Basis of Claim are not explained by the Appellant's profession as a XXXX

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred on credibility findings; the court disagrees and finds omissions not explained by profession.

propositions.text: The RPD made credibility findings based on omissions and contradictions between the BOC and testimony.
propositions.quote: The RPD made credibility findings based on the omission of material facts from the Appellant's BOC and contradictions between the Appellant's BOC and his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found credibility issues due to omissions and contradictions between the BOC and testimony.

propositions.text: The Appellant's profession explains omissions due to memory loss and confusion, causing gaps in recalling details.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that the Appellant's background as a professional XXXX explains omissions from his BOC: We respectfully submit that the Claimant, as a XXXX, exhibited at the hearing clear signs of memory loss and confusion. Any reasonable person would comprehend that a professional with that background could have certain gaps in remembering and recalling. Thus it is understandable that the Claimant, at the time of preparing his statement and his BOC may have omitted details and circumstances of his flight to Nigeria [sic], which took place years before he reached Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues his profession caused memory loss and confusion explaining omissions in his BOC.

propositions.text: The court rejects the Appellant's argument that omissions are explained by his profession or cognitive impairment at hearing.
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's argument on appeal that omissions in his BOC are explained by the Appellant's profession as a boxer. I have examined the transcript and listened to the audio recording of the hearing. I do not agree that the Appellant showed clear signs of cognitive impairment at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: The Appellant was represented by Counsel when completing his BOC and at the RPD hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was represented by Counsel when he completed his BOC and at the RPD hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the Appellant's explanation of omissions due to profession or impairment and notes he was represented by Counsel.

propositions.text: Appellant's Counsel did not request vulnerable person status or accommodation at the RPD hearing.
propositions.quote: Appellant's Counsel did not request that the Appellant be considered a vulnerable person nor did Counsel request accommodation at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: No record supports treating the Appellant as a vulnerable person at the RPD hearing.
propositions.quote: I find that there is nothing in the record to support a finding that the RPD Panel ought to have treated the Appellant as a vulnerable person.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no request or record supporting treating the Appellant as vulnerable at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not provide medical reports of memory loss or confusion to the RPD or RAD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant did not provide any medical reports to the RPD or to the RAD that he suffers from memory loss and confusion as he argues on appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Appellant provided no medical reports of memory loss or confusion to the RPD or RAD.

propositions.text: The court rejects the Appellant's explanation for omissions and inconsistencies and finds they undermine his credibility.
propositions.quote: I do not accept the Appellant's explanation that and omissions in his BOC and inconsistencies between his BOC and his testimony are explained by his past profession. I find that the omissions and inconsistencies undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the Appellant's explanation for omissions and inconsistencies and finds they undermine credibility.

propositions.text: The Appellant testified his father was poisoned in Nigeria in 2017 and family blamed President Buhari.
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified at the RPD hearing that he had been told by his mother that his father had been killed in Nigeria. The Appellant testified that he had been told that his father had been poisoned and the family believed that President Buhari was responsible for his father's death.

propositions.text: The Appellant testified his father criticized President Buhari while in the US.
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that his father had continued to criticize President Buhari when the father was in the US.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant testified his father was poisoned in 2017 and blamed President Buhari, and that his father criticized Buhari in the US.

propositions.text: The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation for omitting father's death details from BOC and found it undermined credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the Appellant why these details of his father's death by poison in 2017 were not included in his BOC. The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation that he thought he had included these details in his BOC and he had mentioned them to his then Counsel. The RPD found that these material allegations undermine the Appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the Appellant's explanation for omitting father's death details and found it undermined credibility.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not err and that omission of father's death details undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD did not err. I find that the details of his father's death, allegedly at the hands of pollical adversaries, are central to the Appellant's claim that his own life would be at risk because of his father's political opinion. I do not accept the Appellant's explanation as to why he did not include the details in his BOC. I find that the omission of the details regarding his father's alleged death by poison in 2017 undermines the Appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error by the RPD and that omitting father's death details undermines the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The RPD found credibility eroded by failure to mention father and brothers' US refugee status and lack of corroborating documents.
propositions.quote: The RPD Panel found that the Appellant's credibility is eroded by the Appellant's failure to mention in his BOC that his father and brothers were granted refugee status in the US. The RPD found that the Appellant's failure to obtain any documents to corroborate their refugee status erodes his credibility. The RPD cites jurisprudence11 that failure to provide documents that the panel would expect to see is an important element in establishing credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's credibility eroded by failure to mention family US refugee status and lack of documents.

propositions.text: The court agrees that family refugee claims are highly relevant to the Appellant's claim.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD. The refugee claim of his father and his brothers are highly relevant to the Appellant's claim. The Appellant is in the US because his father was persecuted in Nigeria based on his political opinion.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees family refugee claims are highly relevant to the Appellant's claim.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant did not establish credible evidence of danger in Nigeria.
propositions.quote: The RPD Panel found that Appellant has not established through sufficient credible evidence that he would be in danger in Nigeria.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD decision wrongly focuses on failure to seek asylum in the US as basis for rejection.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that "the RPD decision is based almost entirely on the fact that the Claimant did not formally seek asylum. Once again, the RPD Member seems to presume that if there were a true danger, the Claimant would have taken every single measure to ensure protection by the United States so as to prevent returning to Nigeria."

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no credible evidence of danger in Nigeria; the Appellant argues the RPD wrongly focused on failure to seek asylum in the US.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues he relied on boxing promoters and wife to regularize US status but was unsuccessful.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that he relied upon his boxing promoters to regularize his immigration status in the US and that they did not do so. The Appellant argues on appeal that he attempted to obtain legal status in the US though his wife, a US citizen, but he was unsuccessful.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues he unsuccessfully relied on promoters and wife to regularize his US immigration status.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not err and notes the RPD did not base findings on failure to claim asylum in the US.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD did not err, I note that the RPD did not make a finding with respect to the Appellant's subjective fear of persecution in Nigeria based on his failure to claim in the US as the Appellant argues on appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error by the RPD and notes it did not base findings on failure to claim asylum in the US.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues he fears persecution due to father's political opinion and return of persecutor to power in 2019.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that: The Claimant left Nigeria as a young man because he feared persecution for his father and for himself as bis father male heir. He said he also clearly testified that, as circumstances had it, the agent of persecution of 1987 was retuned [sic] to power in 2019. We submit that this fact alone, in the context of the NDP for Nigeria showing the poor record to protect human rights and the concerns for dissidents and opponents, established a considerable and even substantial fear of persecution or at least fear of torture.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues he fears persecution due to his father's political opinion and return of persecutor to power in 2019.

propositions.text: The Appellant has not shown objective evidence of persecution or torture risk due to his father's imprisonment 30 years ago.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with the Appellant that the objective facts establish a fear of persecution or of torture. The Appellant has not referenced any objective evidence that someone who has been out of Nigeria for 30 years would face persecution and torture in Nigeria because his father was imprisoned during the military regime in the 1980s.

propositions.text: The National Documentation Package contains no evidence supporting risk due to the Appellant's father's opposition to the military government.
propositions.quote: I have canvassed the documents in the latest National Documentation Package (NDP) and I find no evidence to support a finding that the Appellant would be at risk because his father opposed the military government in the 1980s.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no objective evidence or documentation supporting the Appellant's fear of persecution or torture due to his father's past imprisonment.

propositions.text: The Appellant submitted a 2017 newspaper article stating his father's burial was delayed because the Appellant is considered 'at large' in Nigeria.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submitted into evidence an article from the XXXX XXXX newspaper, dated XXXX XXXX, 20I7 that says that the Appellant's father's burial has been delayed because the Appellant is considered "at large" in Nigeria.

propositions.text: The article states the Appellant may be arrested and required to answer charges against his father in court.
propositions.quote: The articles states that the Appellant may be arrested and required to answer the charges against his father in court in his father's place.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submitted a 2017 newspaper article alleging his father's burial delay and possible arrest in Nigeria.

propositions.text: The Appellant testified at the RPD that his mother sent him the article and he knew its contents for about two years.
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified at the RPD that his mother had sent him the article and that he had been aware of its contents for about two years.

propositions.text: The RPD asked why the allegations in the article were not in the BOC narrative; the Appellant said he did not know but gave the article to former Counsel.
propositions.quote: The RPD Panel asked the Appellant why the allegations in the newspaper article do not form part of his BOC narrative. The Appellant testified that he did not know why he did not tell his former Counsel about the article when they prepared his BOC form but that he did give a copy of the newspaper article to his former Counsel.

propositions.text: The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation and found the allegations highly material and failure to mention them undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation. The RPD found that the allegations in the article, if they are true, are highly material to the Appellant's claim. The RPD found that failure to mention the allegations undermines the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The RPD gave no weight to the article due to the Appellant's failure to mention it in his BOC.
propositions.quote: The RPD gave no weight to the document given the Appellant's failure to mention the allegation or the article in his BOC.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's failure to mention a material newspaper article undermined his credibility and gave the article no weight.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant cannot rely on the newspaper article to support key claim elements.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD. I find that the Appellant cannot rely on XXXX XXXX XXXX newspaper article to support key elements of his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant cannot rely on the newspaper article to support key claim elements.

propositions.text: The Appellant submitted a 1987 newspaper article stating his father was detained without trial for three years and suspected poisoned in prison.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submitted into evidence an article from the XXXX XXXX XXXX, dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 1987. The article states that the Appellant's father, along with other Nigerian politicians, was detained without trial for three years. The article contains a direct quote from the Appellant in which the Appellant unequivocally states that he suspected that his father had been poisoned while in prison and that the authorities were trying to kill his father.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submitted a 1987 article stating his father was detained without trial and suspected poisoned in prison.

propositions.text: The RPD asked the Appellant about being interviewed for the article; the Appellant denied being interviewed.
propositions.quote: When the RPD Panel asked the Appellant about being interviewed for the article, the Appellant testified that he had not been interviewed for the article.

propositions.text: The RPD noted a direct quote attributed to the Appellant in the article; the Appellant said the quote was from others including his brothers.
propositions.quote: When the RPD Panel put to the Appellant that there is a direct quote attributed to him in the article, the Appellant explained the quote attributed to him was what others were saying, including his brothers.

propositions.text: The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation and found the article should be given no weight due to contradiction.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not accept this explanation and found that the article should not be given any weight given the contradiction.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the Appellant's denial of an interview and gave no weight to the contradictory newspaper article.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues on appeal that a person can be quoted without being interviewed; 'interview' has a broader journalistic meaning.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues on appeal that a person could be quoted in a newspaper article without necessarily being "interviewed". The Appellant argues that the word interview can have a broader meaning in journalism.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues that being quoted does not necessarily mean being interviewed, as 'interview' can have a broader meaning.

propositions.text: The newspaper article was submitted by the Appellant and quotes him stating his father was poisoned in prison.
propositions.quote: I note that the newspaper article in question was submitted by the Appellant. The quote attributed to the Appellant in the article states that his father was poisoned while in prison.

propositions.text: The Appellant's BOC narrative states his father was poisoned after prison but does not mention poisoning in prison.
propositions.quote: The Appellants' BOC narrative states that his father was poisoned after he was released from prison but makes no mention that his father was poisoned in prison.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Appellant submitted the article quoting him about poisoning in prison, differing from his BOC narrative.

propositions.text: The article's evidentiary value is seriously eroded by the Appellant's denial of the interview and differing poisoning narrative.
propositions.quote: I find that the evidentiary value of the newspaper article is seriously eroded by the fact that the article refers to an interview with the Appellant that the Appellant says he did not give, and the narrative of the father's poisoning in the newspaper article differs materially from the Appellant's BOC and testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the article's evidentiary value seriously eroded by contradictions and denial of interview.

propositions.text: The Appellant cannot rely on the 1987 article to support key elements of his claim.
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant cannot rely on the XXXX XXXX XXXX article to support key elements of his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant cannot rely on the 1987 article to support key claim elements.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant is not credible in his claim.
propositions.quote: I agree with he RPD and I find that the Appellant is not credible in his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant is not credible.

propositions.text: There is no serious possibility the Appellant would be persecuted in his country of nationality.
propositions.quote: Having considered all of the evidence before me, I find that there is not a serious possibility that the Appellant would be persecuted in his country of nationality.

propositions.text: On a balance of probabilities, the Appellant would not face torture, risk to life, or cruel and unusual treatment in his country.
propositions.quote: I further find that, on a balance of probabilities, that the Appellant would not be subjected personally to a danger of torture, nor would he face a risk to his life, or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, in his country of nationality.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no serious possibility of persecution or torture risk to the Appellant in his country.

propositions.text: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision denying refugee or protection status.
